name: Money
description: Every account, card, loan and bill in one place: net worth, limits, and what is due next.
dataHelp: Amounts are plain numbers in dollars (22100, not "$22,100"). Dates are "YYYY-MM-DD"; times are full ISO date-times.
accounts: a list. Each account is { id, source, kind, institution, name, balance, updatedAt } plus optional limit, apr, note, payment.
- id: unique text. For one added by hand use "m" followed by digits (e.g. "m1791250000000").
- source: "manual" for anything added by hand or by you; "plaid" for accounts the bank fills in.
- kind: "checking", "savings", "investment", "credit" (a credit card) or "loan" (student loan, car loan, Affirm plan...).
- institution: the company's name, spelled the usual way ("Earnest", "MOHELA", "Capital One", "American Express", "Affirm").
- balance: always positive. For credit cards and loans it is the amount owed; the page shows owed money in brackets itself.
- updatedAt: set it to the current date-time whenever you change a balance, or the page will say it needs updating.
- limit: a credit card's credit limit. apr: the interest rate as a percent number (5.2). note: a few words ("4 payments left").
- payment: the next payment on a card or loan, { amount, due, monthly: true }.
- Accounts with source "plaid" are refreshed from the bank every time the page opens: do not change their balance, it would be overwritten. Adding a limit the bank does not share is fine.
bills: a list of bills that are not an account (insurance, phone, subscriptions). Each is { id, provider, name, sub, amount, due, monthly }.
- id: "b" followed by digits. provider and name: the company ("Liberty Mutual"). sub: what it is ("car insurance"). due: the next due date. monthly: true when it repeats every month.
Marking a bill or payment paid: when monthly, move due forward one month and set lastPaid to today's date; otherwise set paid to today's date.
history, banks, institutions and checkedAt are written by the page itself: leave them alone. settings holds staleDays, warnPct and alertPct (the card-limit warning points).
